# FDG8055

> DO override `Object.Equals` whenever implementing `IEquatable<T>`.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.6 IComparable&lt;T> and IEquatable&lt;T>.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (full coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1067
- Automatic fix: yes
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: draft

CA1067 reports a type that implements IEquatable<T> without overriding Object.Equals, for classes and structs of any accessibility (probe with SDK 10.0.402). Its code fix adds an Equals(object) override that calls Equals(T) (probe), which keeps the two overloads' semantics the same, as the body asks, and changes no signature.

## From the book

Both overloads of the `Equals` method should have exactly the same semantics.

```csharp
public struct PositiveInt32 : IEquatable<PositiveInt32> {
  public bool Equals(PositiveInt32 other) { ... }
  public override bool Equals(object obj){
    if (!obj is PositiveInt32) return false;
    return Equals((PositiveInt32)obj);
  }
}
```
